messages:
alex: Heads-up — we started seeing a chunk of traffic for /v1/* get matched to the Dedicated pool and the X-Client-Id header is getting stripped. Several tenants (acme-corp included) hit 503s. Rolling an emergency priority override now. ping ops.

mira: Which tenants specifically? Any logs/ids?

sam: spike shows tenant=acme-corp, 5xx from dedicated workers, response body 'missing X-Client-Id'.

jen: Confirmed on dashboards. Recent route-priority bump moved the generic /v1/* rule above the header-preserve rule. That ordering is the culprit. Need a hotfix to force preserve for affected hosts.

alex: I'll add a targeted override scoped to acme-corp to preserve headers and raise match priority. Doing it via admin API to avoid a full deploy.

alex: Command I'm running:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/routing/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOK" \
  -d '{"name":"emergency-preserve-acme","match":{"host":"acme-corp","path_prefix":"/v1/"},"rewrite":null,"priority":100,"preserve_headers":["X-Client-Id","Authorization"]}'
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: override applied id=ovr-20260318-01 by alex. propagation started (~17s).

mira: Running quick curl via staging gateway to verify.

sam: test -> 200, headers present, latency back to baseline :thumbsup:

jen: Good. Next steps: create a canary in console for acme only, then schedule a proper config rollback or permanent rule change in infra repo. Also need a rollback playbook documented.

alex: Adding rollback command here: 
```
curl -X DELETE "https://admin.internal/api/v1/routing/overrides/ovr-20260318-01" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOK"
```

deploy-bot: infra: scheduled config-rollout job queued (reconcile overrides) for 01:00 UTC.

mira: I'm filing an incident ticket and starting a short postmortem. Assigning owners: @jen for RCA/console UX, @sam for telemetry/alerts.

sam: Question — should we alert if route_priority ordering drifts by >10 across prod? This seems to be a recurring footgun.

alex: Yes, add a telemetry rule for route-priority-drift >= 10 and an alert if header-preserve rules are shadowed by generic matches.

jen: Noted. Postmortem will include: playbook for emergency overrides, a console safety overlay when creating priorities that conflict with header-preserve rules, and an automation to detect shadowed rules.

alex: Thanks. Leaving the override in place until the canary and config change land. Will update this thread when we revert/complete the postmortem.
